about: The role table: what each kind of object IS and what treatments it needs. Roles may name example things (slate, barrel) because this is data, never code. A role is "class.name". The class decides which treatments are REQUIRED (the audit fails without them) and which are WANTED (the audit says look). Each role carries a surface id (data/surfaces.json), a displace flag (real displacement only where true), may_hang (a part hung from above is allowed), needs_support (ground: stands on the ground, part: carried by another part, none), max_span_metres (the longest free span of a plank or beam), scale (fact ids in data/real_world_facts.json), dials (multipliers per wear layer, 0 = the layer is not for this role), exempt (treatments the role does not need, with the reason) a meaning (one plain line: what the role is for; `explainer-film-place roles --list` prints them all) and name_hints (regular expressions that guess the role from an object, collection or material name when the settings say nothing). Numbers in a role (max_span_metres, dials) share the role's own kind and source. A treatment is REQUIRED only if the kit really makes it and a test proves it (check-presets enforces this).
